findings.failureScenario: SyncCommit detects an Undo or edit made between its own steps only by comparing undo.len() with the length after its last step. Session::commit caps the undo stack at 1000 (lib.rs:516 removes the oldest entry), so once the history is full every commit leaves undo.len() unchanged; likewise an Undo followed by one edit restores the same length. In the app the SyncWork runs on a worker while the UI thread keeps accepting edits: with a full history, import batch committed -> user edits a photo -> Relink step committed, after_last == undo.len() so interleaved stays false, and finish() merges the last `own` (2) entries = [user edit, relink] into one 'Synchronize Folder' step. Undoing Synchronize Folder then also reverts the user's unrelated edit, contrary to the documented contract that an edit made meanwhile stays its own step.
findings.action: Track interleaving with the monotonic s.commits() counter (record commits after each own step and flag interleaved when it differs on entry) plus an undo-pop counter, instead of undo.len().
findings.sourceQuote: they are merged only while nothing else came in between (an Undo or an edit made meanwhile stays its own step, and the run's parts stay theirs).

findings.failureScenario: migrate(Move) deletes the source when a valid proxy already exists at the destination. The only same-folder guard is the lexical `new_dir == current` PathBuf comparison in smart_location (previews.rs). On macOS/Windows case-insensitive volumes, or via a symlink or a `..` spelling, the user can pick the same folder under another spelling (e.g. `/Users/a/Pictures/smart previews` for `/Users/a/Pictures/Smart Previews`). Then for every proxy dst resolves to the same file as src, is_valid(&dst) is true and std::fs::remove_file(&src) deletes it: every smart preview is lost and counted as 'moved'. Smart previews are the only editable copy while originals are offline, so photos on an unplugged drive become uneditable.
findings.action: Before removing src, skip when src and dst are the same file (compare canonicalized paths or (dev, inode)/file id), and have smart_location compare canonicalized directories rather than PathBuf equality.

anchor.text: // ±1° covers 50 km everywhere except very near the poles (where there are no cities)

findings.failureScenario: reverse() searches only the 3x3 block of 1-degree cells. One degree of longitude is 111 km x cos(lat), under MAX_KM (50 km) above about 63.3 degrees latitude, where cities15000 does list places (Tromso 69.6N, Murmansk 68.9N, Reykjavik 64.1N, Fairbanks 64.8N). A photo at 69.65N, 18.02E sits in cell 18; a place at 69.65N, 16.95E is about 41 km west, within MAX_KM, but lies in cell 16 (dx = -2) and is never examined, so the lookup returns a farther place in the 3x3 block or nothing.
findings.action: Widen the longitude search to ceil(MAX_KM / (111.32 km x cos(lat))) cells (clamped, with wrap) instead of a fixed +-1.
findings.sourceQuote: Lookups farther than this from any place find nothing.
